articles.title: EU AI Watch: 'TypeSafe AI's Mega-Round: A Glimpse into Europe's AI Future'
articles.excerpt: An $870 million round landed in Europe this week, and the number on the check wasn't the most interesting part. The most interesting part was what the company was actually selling: AI that doesn't qui…
articles.body: An $870 million round landed in Europe this week, and the number on the check wasn't the most interesting part. The most interesting part was what the company was actually selling: AI that doesn't quietly break. TypeSafe AI, a European startup working on type-safe AI systems, closed a mega-round valuing it at $7.5 billion. For context, that's the kind of money that normally shows up for chip fabs and foundation-model labs. Here it went to a company whose entire pitch is reliability — systems designed to fail predictably, catch errors before they propagate, and avoid the classic LLM failure mode of confidently doing something catastrophic with your bank account. That distinction matters more than it used to.

articles.body: I had four 8-inch tablets lying in a drawer. No-name hardware, the kind you buy because it is cheap and then forget about. At the same time, the tablets I already use as Home Assistant wall panels were driving me mad: the kiosk browser would sometimes simply not be in the foreground anymore, even though it was configured to stay there, and the one in the hallway regularly ended up showing a blank white page until I rebooted it. So the question was: can I turn these drawer tablets into wall panels that are boringly reliable ? Slim system, screen always on, Home Assistant as the only thing that ever runs, brightness controlled from Home Assistant. And if I bricked one along the way — fine, they were destined for the bin anyway.

articles.title: How to Differential-Test LLM Routing Changes
articles.excerpt: An LLM router can return the same final 200 response after making a very different decision. It may choose another deployment, add a retry, cross a provider boundary, consume a fallback, or start a st…
articles.body: An LLM router can return the same final 200 response after making a very different decision. It may choose another deployment, add a retry, cross a provider boundary, consume a fallback, or start a stream before a later failure. A status-code comparison will miss those regressions. Differential testing runs the same case against a reference router and a candidate router, normalizes their observable results, and compares the behaviors that must remain stable.

articles.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
articles.excerpt: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its stellar companion.
articles.body: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean.
